chunks: He who suspects wrong or partiality on the part of the testator and brings about a settlement, does not incur any guilt, for God is verily forgiving and merciful.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one fears injustice in a will?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this verse (2:182) establishes the permissibility of *sulh* (conciliation) in wills to correct deviations from justice, serving as a specific exception to the general rule of strict adherence to the testator's instructions. It highlights the scholarly principle that preserving family harmony and preventing sin outweighs rigid formalism, with the divine attribute of Mercy underscoring the validity of such corrective measures.
